profile.summary: trRosettaRNA predicts the full-atom 3D structure of an RNA from its sequence. It takes a multiple sequence alignment and a secondary structure, uses a transformer network to predict inter-nucleotide distances, orientations and backbone torsion angles, and then folds a 3D model by energy minimisation in Rosetta. The output is a PDB file.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; package README: Overview, Usage

summary_quotes.text: The trRosettaRNA pipeline comprises two major steps: 1D and 2D geometries prediction by a transformer network; and 3D structure folding by energy minimization.
output PDB file storing the predicted 3D structure

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: For a query RNA, an MSA is built (with rMSA, or Infernal against RNAcentral) and a secondary structure is predicted with SPOT-RNA. These are turned into an MSA representation and a pair representation, which also carries direct couplings from the MSA and the secondary structure probability matrix. A transformer called RNAformer, similar to the Evoformer in AlphaFold2, updates both representations. A single pass has 48 blocks, cycled 4 times. It outputs probability distributions for 1D torsion angles and 2D distances, contacts and orientations. These are converted into restraints that, with physics-based Rosetta energy terms, guide energy minimisation to full-atom models; the package generates several decoys and keeps the one with minimum energy.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two releases of the standalone package are named. Version 1.0 is the version used in the Nature Communications paper, downloadable from the lab website. Version 1.1, on Zenodo (record 10616895, 2024-02-03), adds support for custom secondary structure files. The package ships one RNAformer checkpoint, params/model_1, used by default. For its benchmarks the paper trained separate models on date-filtered training sets to avoid leakage; those are not described as released. A result should name the package version, the MSA tool and database, and the secondary structure source, since the authors report sensitivity to secondary structure quality.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Automated deep learning pipeline for RNA 3D structure prediction: a transformer predicts geometries, then Rosetta energy minimisation builds the model.

quotes.text: an automated deep learning-based approach to RNA 3D structure prediction

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: RNAformer transformer (Evoformer-like, 48 blocks cycled 4 times) acting on MSA and pair representations, followed by restraint-guided energy minimisation with Rosetta energy terms.

energy minimization with deep learning potentials and physics-based energy terms in Rosetta

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: An MSA in A3M format and the sequence in FASTA. A secondary structure is predicted by SPOT-RNA automatically, or given as a dot-bracket, ct or SPOT-RNA .prob file (v1.1).

limitations.text: The authors state that accuracy depends on the quality of the predicted secondary structure, is limited on novel RNAs, and that synthetic RNAs remain hard.

quotes.text: First, the performance of trRosettaRNA is susceptible to the quality of predicted secondary structures. Secondly, though trRosettaRNA achieves promising accuracy in the internal benchmark tests, its performance on novel RNAs remains limited. Moreover, the automated structure prediction of synthetic RNAs remains challenging.

run_guide.summary: Download the trRosettaRNA v1.1 package from Zenodo, install its environment and PyRosetta, and predict the bundled example with its supplied MSA and dot-bracket secondary structure.
prerequisites: conda; the linux.yml environment uses Python 3.8, PyTorch 1.11.0 and cudatoolkit 11.3.1 (linux-cu102.yml for CUDA 10.x).
The RosettaCommons conda channel added before installing PyRosetta; PyRosetta's own licence terms apply.
A GPU is optional for predict.py (the default -gpu -1 is CPU only); folding runs on CPU.
SPOT-RNA in its own Python 3.6 environment, only if no secondary structure file is supplied.

notes: No official GitHub repository exists for trRosettaRNA v1; several GitHub mirrors (for example yss-THU/trRosettaRNA_v1.1, LunaLau0/trRosettaRNA_v1.1) were seen in search and not used. A successor, YangLab-SDU/trRosettaRNA2, exists and may deserve its own record; it was not read. The v1.1 zip (172,235,702 bytes) was downloaded to extract two files and then deleted; only the README and linux.yml are kept. The package-readme and package-env sources have the zip as artifact_url, while their sha256 is of the extracted member file, so a re-fetch of the URL will not match the hash without extracting trRosettaRNA_v1.1/README and trRosettaRNA_v1.1/linux.yml first.
